description: A three-panel composite figure validating a dynamic-recrystallization (DRX) grain-size prediction model. (a) is a line-and-marker plot of grain size (µm, y axis 0-80) versus Temperature (°C, x axis 900-1150), with four series for strain rates 0.01 s⁻¹ (black squares), 0.1 s⁻¹ (red circles), 1 s⁻¹ (blue triangles) and 10 s⁻¹ (magenta stars); a solid line labelled "Experimental grain size" joins the points of each series. Grain size rises monotonically with temperature for every strain rate, and the slower the strain rate the coarser the grain: at 1150 °C the 0.01 s⁻¹ series reaches just below the 80 µm gridline while the 10 s⁻¹ series stays near 25 µm; at 900 °C all series lie between roughly 8 and 13 µm. (b) plots predicted grain size (y) against experimental grain size (x), both axes 0-80 µm; open circles are "Data points", a blue dashed line is the "Linear fit of data points", and two red lines bracket ±10 % deviation, annotated "Positive deviation is 10%" and "Negative deviation is 10%". Printed inside: R = 0.996, MRE = 4.53 %. (c) plots absolute error (µm, 0-7.5) against experimental grain size (µm, 0-80) with a dashed horizontal line at 3.0 µm. The figure demonstrates that the model reproduces measured DRX average grain size with high correlation and errors mostly inside 3 µm.

subfigures.description: Grain size (µm, 0-80) versus Temperature (900-1150 °C) for four strain rates (0.01, 0.1, 1, 10 s⁻¹, marked by black squares, red circles, blue triangles, magenta stars) with a solid line labelled 'Experimental grain size'. Grain size increases with temperature for all curves and is largest at the lowest strain rate.

Scatter plot of predicted grain size versus experimental grain size (both axes 0-80 µm); open circles are 'Data points', blue dashed line is the 'Linear fit of data points', and two red lines bound ±10 % deviation (annotated 'Positive deviation is 10 %' / 'Negative deviation is 10 %'). Printed statistics: R = 0.996, MRE = 4.53 %.

Absolute error (µm, 0-7.5) versus experimental grain size (µm, 0-80) as open circles, with a blue dashed line at 3.0 µm indicating the error threshold; most points fall below the line, with one point above 3 µm near ~4.2 µm.

observations.observation: Panel (a) plots grain size (µm) against temperature from 900 to 1150 °C at four strain rates, and every curve rises monotonically with increasing temperature.
In panel (a) the grain size at a given temperature increases as the strain rate decreases: 0.01 s⁻¹ gives the largest grains, 10 s⁻¹ the smallest.
Legend entries in panel (a) are a solid line labelled 'Experimental grain size' plus markers for 0.01 s⁻¹, 0.1 s⁻¹, 1 s⁻¹ and 10 s⁻¹.
In panel (a) the 0.01 s⁻¹ point at 1150 °C lies just below the 80 µm gridline, while the 10 s⁻¹ point at the same temperature lies near 25 µm.
Panel (b) plots predicted grain size against experimental grain size on identical 0-80 µm axes, with open-circle data points closely tracking the dashed linear fit.
Panel (b) contains two red boundary lines annotated 'Positive deviation is 10 %' and 'Negative deviation is 10 %', bracketing the linear fit.
Panel (c) plots absolute error (µm) versus experimental grain size (µm) and includes a dashed horizontal line at 3.0 µm; most data points lie below that line.
The caption states the figure shows the correlation and absolute error between predicted and experimental values of the dynamic recrystallization grain size model.
The citing text states that R is 0.996 and MRE for all samples is only 4.53 %, indicating a high degree of coincidence between predicted and experimental grain size.
The citing text states that the absolute error between predicted and experimental grain size values is mostly within 3 µm.

The citing text attributes model errors to competing effects during dynamic recrystallization (grain growth promoted by temperature and plastic strain versus refinement by DRX) plus statistical error, and claims the model provides a reliable theoretical basis for predicting DRX grain size of low-density high-strength steel after hot forging.
